issue.title: 4.7: Silence MapView production logs
issue.body_excerpt: Remove or gate console.log of domains and geo payloads.

affected_files.role: primary - currently has 2 console.error (lines 88, 374) for fetch/cache error paths; the issue specifically calls out 'console.log of domains and geo payloads'. Grepping the file shows NO console.log (only console.error). Acceptance says 'MapView.jsx has no unconditional console.log' — already true. The two console.error calls are conditional (catch blocks) and acceptable to keep, but if the maintainer wants stricter hygiene, they can be wrapped in a debug-guard. Recommend: leave console.error untouched, document the finding as already-resolved by the codebase's existing discipline, and close the issue with a one-line PR that removes the comments / debug-prints if any. If the issue is interpreted strictly ('no console.log of domains and geo payloads'), there's nothing to do — verify `rg -n 'console.log' src/dashboard/components/MapView.jsx` exits 1 (already true).

analysis.current_implementation: MapView.jsx has two console.error calls (line 88 'MapView: Error fetching geolocation data', line 374 'Error clearing cache'). No console.log, no console.warn, no console.info. The issue title says 'console.log of domains and geo payloads' but the file contains none.
analysis.limitations: The acceptance is already met. The two console.error calls are in catch blocks (justified) and are not 'logs of domains or geo payloads' — they are error messages. The pragmatic interpretation: the issue was filed on an earlier version of the file (before the console.logs were removed in a prior P1/P2 PR), and the current state is clean.
analysis.change_surface: 0-1 file. If we accept the issue as already-resolved, the action is a comment in the PR that the verify command exits 1 today. If the maintainer wants stricter hygiene, wrap the two console.error calls behind `if (import.meta.env?.DEV)` or a debug flag — one tiny change.
analysis.root_cause: The original P0/P1 codebase had console.log calls in MapView for dev debugging; they were removed in a later pass (F-UX-004). The issue is now a no-op — the verify command already exits 1.

options.name: Close as already-resolved
options.summary: Open a one-line PR (or no-PR close) noting that `rg -n 'console.log' src/dashboard/components/MapView.jsx` already exits 1. The two remaining console.error calls are in catch blocks and are justified. If desired, gate them behind a debug flag — but it's optional polish.
pros: Zero risk; matches the actual code state
cons: Some PR workflows require a code change to close an issue — in that case, gate the console.error behind a debug flag in one line
options.risk_details: No behavior change if closed as-is; one-line optional guard otherwise.

options.name: Gate the two console.error behind a debug flag
options.summary: Introduce a small `debugLog` helper or guard the two console.error calls behind `if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.__EFP_DEBUG__)`. Defensive, but adds a line for no real benefit since they are already catch-block error prints (not domain/geo payload dumps).
pros: Production console is silent even in error paths (matches 'silence' interpretation)
cons: Hides real errors from the user/console — anti-pattern for an extension where the only feedback channel IS the console
options.risk_details: Optional polish. Verify the issue's `rg -n 'console.log' src/dashboard/components/MapView.jsx` exits 1 either way.

options_considered: Gate the two console.error behind a debug flag
options_rejected: Gate the console.error — hides real errors, anti-pattern for an extension
